title: Chapter 15: The Elegant Flirt 5
content:
Chapter 15

The Elegant Flirt 5

Wei Wuxian was a master at entertaining himself, especially when it came to making the best of a miserable situation. Since there was nothing else to play with, he’d just have to play with Lan Wangji.

"Wangji-xiong," he called out.

Lan Wangji remained an immovable rock.

"Wangji."

Deaf to the world.

"Lan Wangji."

"Lan Zhan!"

Lan Wangji finally set his brush down, lifting a glacial stare.

Wei Wuxian shrank back in mock defense, hands held up like a shield. "Hey, don't look at me like that! I tried calling you 'Wangji' and you blew me off, so I had to use your birth name. If it bothers you that much, you're free to call me by mine."

Lan Wangji’s voice was clipped. "Put your leg down."

Wei Wuxian’s posture was atrocious—slumped to one side, an elbow propped on the desk, one knee jacked up on the mat. Seeing that his prodding had finally cracked that stone facade felt like watching the sun break through a storm. Grinning, he obliged and dropped his leg, though he immediately leaned his upper body even closer, resting his forearms against the wood. Still a complete disgrace to proper etiquette.

He leaned in, wearing a ridiculously earnest expression. "Lan Zhan, honest question: do you... really hate my guts that much?"

Lan Wangji merely lowered his lashes, casting faint shadows over his pale, jade-carved cheeks.

"Come on!" Wei Wuxian whined. "Two words in and you're back to ignoring me? I’m actually trying to apologize here, cross my heart! Just look at me."

When the silence stretched, he shrugged. "Fine, don't look. I'll just say my piece anyway. The other night—that was on me. My bad. I shouldn't have hopped your fence, I shouldn't have smuggled liquor, and I definitely shouldn't have picked a fight with you. But I swear! I wasn't doing it to provoke you on purpose. I honestly hadn't read your clan rules! In the Jiang clan, our rules are just common sense passed down by word of mouth—nobody writes them down on a rock. If I'd known, I wouldn't have done it!"

I definitely wouldn't have downed that jar of Emperor’s Smile right in front of your face, he thought silently. I would've tucked it into my robes, snuck it back to my room, and sipped it in secret—every single night, passing jars out to the whole crew until we drank the town dry.

Wei Wuxian pressed on, tapping the wood to make his point. "And let's be fair here: who threw the first punch? You did! If you hadn't swung on me, we could've talked things out like civilized gentlemen. But someone draws a sword on me, I have to defend myself, right? You can't put the whole blame on my shoulders. Lan Zhan, are you even listening to me? Hey. Look at me. Young Master Lan?" He snapped his fingers right in the boy's face. "Second Brother Lan! Cut me some slack and give me a glance, huh?"

Without bothering to lift his eyes, Lan Wangji flatly delivered his verdict: "Copy it one more time."

Wei Wuxian’s spine melted, flopping sideways in despair. "Don't be like that! I'm saying I'm sorry!"

"You don't harbor a single shred of remorse," Lan Wangji countered, entirely ruthless.

Wei Wuxian ditched every ounce of his pride without hesitation. "I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I'm sorry! I'll say it as many times as you want! I'll get on my knees and say it if that’ll make you happy!"

Lan Wangji set his brush aside. Wei Wuxian braced himself, thinking the guy had finally cracked and was getting ready to throw hands. He opened his mouth, winding up a cheeky grin, only to find his lips glued shut like solid wax. The smile froze dead.

His eyes went wide in panic. "Mmh?! Mmh-mmh-mmh!"

Lan Wangji shut his eyes, exhaling a quiet breath. When he opened them, the tranquil, untouchable stillness had returned. He picked up his brush and went back to work, as though nothing had happened. Wei Wuxian had heard plenty about the maddening cruelty of the Lan Clan’s Silence Spell, but he refused to believe he couldn't crack it. He clawed at his mouth and rubbed his jaw until his skin flared red, yet his lips wouldn't part an inch.

Furious, he snatched a fresh sheet of paper, his brush flying across the fibers, and tossed the note across the desk.

Lan Wangji glanced down, murmured, "Absurd," and crumpled the paper into a tight ball before chucking it aside.

Seething, Wei Wuxian rolled across the woven mat like a petulant toddler, scrambled back up, furiously scribbled a second note, and slammed it face-up right before the boy.

Crumple. Gone.

The Silence Spell held firm until the incense burned down and his daily copying shift came to an end. By the time Wei Wuxian returned the next morning, the floor was clean—every crumpled paper ball had vanished.

Wei Wuxian was the poster child for never learning his lesson. Barely fifteen minutes into the quiet, his tongue started itching again. He recklessly tossed out a couple of lines, only to get slapped with the Silence Spell on the spot. Muzzled, he resorted to manic scribbles, sliding sheet after sheet across the desk—which Lan Wangji methodically balled up and pitched onto the floor. Day three went down the exact same way.

After days of enduring this recurring gag, the final day of his library detention arrived. And to Lan Wangji’s surprise, Wei Wuxian walked in looking like an entirely different person.

Since arriving in Gusu, his sword had been left lying around random corners—nobody had ever caught him properly wearing it. Yet today, he marched in with the scabbard strapped to his hip, slamming it down beside his desk with a loud clatter. Far from his usual routine of relentless teasing, he didn't utter a peep. He sat down, dipped his brush, and set straight to work. The obedience was downright unnerving.

With no justification to mute him, Lan Wangji found his gaze lingering on the boy, deeply skeptical of this sudden burst of model behavior. Sure enough, fifteen minutes hadn't even passed before Wei Wuxian relapsed. He slid a sheet of paper across the wood, tapping a finger to urge him to look.

Expecting another barrage of nonsensical ramblings, Lan Wangji looked down anyway.

It was an ink portrait.

A young man sitting in pristine posture by an open lattice window, quietly reading an ancient scroll. Every line of the brows, the solemn tilt of the chin—it captured his exact likeness down to the soul.

Seeing that Lan Wangji hadn't immediately thrown it out, Wei Wuxian’s lips curved upward. He shot him a cocky wink, his face practically screaming: Dead ringer, right? Pretty impressive, huh?

Lan Wangji spoke slowly, his tone flat. "If you have this much free time, you should be copying texts instead of scribbling nonsense. Clearly, you have no desire to ever leave this room."

Wei Wuxian blew gently across the wet ink, entirely unfazed. "I've already finished the whole stack. Tomorrow, I'm a free man!"

The slender fingers resting against the parchment froze for a fraction of a second before turning the page. Oddly enough, he didn't silence him.

Seeing that the bait wasn't sparking a reaction, Wei Wuxian tossed the drawing onto the mat with a casual flick. "Keep it. Gift from me."

The portrait fluttered onto the reed mat, ignored. Over the past month, every note Wei Wuxian had written—taunts, flattery, dramatic apologies, desperate pleas, and idle doodles—had met the exact same fate. Wei Wuxian was long used to it, but just as he sat back, he perked up. "Wait, I forgot! One last touch."

He snatched the parchment back, dipped his brush, and added three quick strokes. Holding the portrait up against the living model, he dissolved into helpless snickers, rolling flat onto his back.

Lan Wangji set his scroll aside and glanced over.

There, tucked over the ear of the inked portrait, sat a delicate, blooming flower.

The corner of Lan Wangji’s lip gave a microscopic twitch.

Scrambling upright, Wei Wuxian cut in before the boy could speak: "'Absurd', right? I knew you’d say absurd. Can you broaden your vocabulary for once? Try tossing in two more syllables!"

Lan Wangji’s voice was pure ice. "Utterly absurd."

Wei Wuxian clapped in mock celebration. "Two more syllables, just like I asked! Much appreciated!"

Lan Wangji pulled his gaze away, picking up the scroll he’d set down and flipping it open.

The second his eyes hit the parchment, he recoiled, hurling the volume away as if he’d been burned by open flame!

It was supposed to be a sacred Buddhist sutra. But the moment he cracked it open, the pages were plastered with naked, tangled bodies writhing in shameless, explicit positions. The sacred scripture had been swapped out for an illustrated erotic novel tucked inside the Buddhist cover.

A toddler could have deduced the culprit. Wei Wuxian had pulled the old switcheroo while distracting him with the sketch. Worse, the culprit wasn't even pretending to hide it—he was pounding the wooden desk, howling with laughter until tears streamed down his cheeks.

The book landed face-up on the floorboards, and Lan Wangji retreated to the corner of the pavilion as if dodging a nest of vipers. His fury finally broke its banks into a thunderous roar:

"Wei Ying—!"

Wei Wuxian was laughing so hard he slid clean off his mat onto the floor. "Present! Sir, yes sir!"

A sharp metallic hiss filled the pavilion as Lan Wangji drew Bichen.

Since setting foot in Gusu, Wei Wuxian had never seen the boy lose his composure this violently. Scrambling to snatch his own sword, he slipped the blade three inches from its scabbard, shouting back, "Etiquette! Second Young Master Lan! Mind your decorum! I brought my blade today—if we wreck this place, how are you explaining it to your uncle?!"

He’d anticipated Lan Wangji blowing a gasket, which was the only reason he’d actually bothered strapping a weapon on: strictly to keep himself from getting accidentally skewered in the crossfire.

Lan Wangji leveled the blade at his chest, pale eyes blazing with unbridled fury. "What kind of creature are you?!"

Wei Wuxian shrugged. "What kind do I look like? A red-blooded man!"

"Shameless degenerate!"

Wei Wuxian snorted. "You're getting prudish over this? Don't tell me you've never flipped through an erotic novel before. Come on, I don't buy it for a second."

Lan Wangji’s fatal flaw was that he had zero repertoire of insults. Choking on his own boiling rage, the frost on his face hardened. He gestured with his sword toward the courtyard. "Outside. We settle this with steel."

Wei Wuxian shook his head violently, putting on his best innocent face. "No way, no chance! Don't you know the rules, Young Master Lan? Private brawling is forbidden in the Cloud Recesses!"

Seeing the tossed book lying in the open, he leaned down to scoop it up, but Lan Wangji closed the distance in a flash, snatching the volume first.

Wei Wuxian’s mind spun, realizing the boy was going to use it as hard evidence to get him expelled. He leaned in, teasing deliberately, "Why the rush to grab it? I thought you weren't interested. Changing your mind? Hey, no need to get grabby—I borrowed it specifically for you anyway! Once you've read my erotic scrolls, that makes us brothers! We can compare notes, trade pointers—I've got way more where that came from..."

Lan Wangji’s face went paper-white. He ground every word out through clenched teeth: "I. Will. Not. Read. It."

Wei Wuxian spun the narrative right on its head. "If you're not reading it, why hold onto it? Stashing it for your private collection? That won't do, brother. I had to borrow that copy; you need to return it when you're done... Whoa, whoa, back off! You're standing way too close, you're making me nervous! Let's talk this out! Wait, you're not planning to hand that in, are you? To who? To old—to your uncle? Second Young Master Lan, you really think you can hand that to the family elders? He's going to assume you read the whole thing first! With skin as thin as yours, you’d die of pure embarrassment..."

Spiritual energy flooded Lan Wangji’s right fist.

Rip—crack!

The book detonated into thousands of fluttering paper shreds, raining down through the air like a blizzard of confetti.

Seeing that his psychological warfare had successfully provoked the boy into destroying the evidence, Wei Wuxian breathed a silent sigh of relief. He put on a tragic, wounded pout. "What a heartbreaking waste of good art!" Plucking a stray scrap of paper from his own bangs, he held it out to the seething Lan Wangji. "You know, Lan Zhan, you're a great guy, but you really need to stop littering. How many paper balls have you pitched at the floor this month? Guess crumpled balls got too boring, so today you moved on to shredded paper! You ripped it, so you clean it up. I'm not touching it."

Naturally, he hadn't swept a single scrap all month anyway.

Lan Wangji’s knuckles turned white around his hilt. Every ounce of his legendary restraint snapped like brittle twig.

"Get the hell out!" he roared.

Wei Wuxian gasped in mock horror. "My, my, Lan Zhan! Everyone praises you as the spotless gentleman, the shining jewel of the mortal realm, the living paragon of decorum—turns out you're just like the rest of us! Don't you know clamoring is forbidden in the Cloud Recesses? And did you really just tell me to 'get the hell out'? Is that the first time you've ever used a four-letter word on someone...?"

Lan Wangji thrust his blade forward.

Wei Wuxian vaulted onto the windowsill in a clean, effortless leap. "Leaving, leaving! Nobody does a strategic retreat quite like me! No need to see me out!"

He dropped straight out the window into the grass below, howling with wild, breathless laughter as he sprinted through the pines.

Waiting in the thicket was a cluster of familiar faces. Nie Huaisang poked his head out, frantic. "Well?! Did he see it? How did he look?!"

Wei Wuxian wiped a tear of laughter from his eye. "How did he look? Man, didn't you hear him screaming across the compound?!"

Nie Huaisang’s jaw dropped in pure veneration. "We heard it! He told you to get the hell out! Brother Wei, I have never in my entire life heard Lan Wangji tell someone to screw off! How on earth did you pull that off?!"

Wei Wuxian puffed his chest out, smug as a peacock. "Rejoice, boys! Today, I personally helped him break his virgin seal on vulgarity! Behold: the legendary Lan family poise and flawless breeding—shattered to pieces before yours truly!"

Jiang Cheng scowled, his face dark as a thundercloud. "Wipe that stupid grin off your face! What the hell are you bragging about?! Is getting screamed at by Lan Wangji some badge of honor? You’re dragging our family’s name through the mud!"

"I went in there with every intention of playing nice," Wei Wuxian argued, clapping a casual arm around Jiang Cheng’s tense shoulders. "He's the one who gave me the cold shoulder! He muzzled me for an entire month—what’s wrong with having a little harmless fun? I even gave him a parting gift out of the goodness of my heart! Though, Huaisang-xiong, I do feel bad about your limited-edition erotic novel. I hadn't even finished reading the good parts! Lan Zhan really doesn't know how to appreciate fine culture—getting worked up over a masterpiece like that. What a waste of that pretty face."

Nie Huaisang waved his fan dismissively. "No harm done! I’ve got plenty more where that came from!"

Jiang Cheng sneered, shoving Wei Wuxian's arm off his shoulder. "You’ve completely alienated both Lan Wangji and Lan Qiren in one go. Just wait until tomorrow—you’re a dead man! Don't expect anyone to collect your corpse."

Wei Wuxian just grinned, slinging his arm right back over Jiang Cheng's neck. "Who cares about tomorrow? Fun comes first! Besides, you’ve cleaned up my messes a hundred times already—what’s one more between brothers?"

Jiang Cheng aimed a kick straight at his shins. "Get lost! Next time you pull this suicidal shit, keep me out of it! And don't you dare invite me to watch!"
